beats.text: A small Spanish town chose death over surrender to Rome.
Numantia was a Celtiberian hill town in the heart of Spain. For twenty years, it beat back Rome's legions again and again.
So Rome sent its most feared general: Scipio Aemilianus, the man who had already destroyed Carthage.
He didn't storm the walls. He built his own wall around the whole town, about nine kilometres long, with towers. And he waited.
No food got in. No one got out. Hunger came, then disease.
When the end came, many Numantines killed themselves rather than become Roman slaves.
Scipio razed what was left. Rome gave him a new name: Numantinus.
Centuries later, Cervantes wrote a tragedy about the siege. In Spanish, numantino still means: resisting to the very end.
